docs.title: Onboard a project from the Projects pillar

beats.act: Open Studio on the Projects pillar
beats.say: The Projects pillar lists every project forge manages. Each card carries the project it stands for, so the operator can pick one without reading the page.
The card is a real link to that project’s own page — the route is the project the previous beat found, not one written down in advance.

beats.act: Go back to the Projects pillar
beats.say: The Projects pillar is one click away from anywhere in Studio.
Onboarding asks for the few things a Factory needs before it can build a repo: what to call it, the quality gate that judges its work, and the north star that tells a planner what it is for.

beats.act: Fill in the name, the quality gate and the north star — and under Advanced, the repo path — then press "Onboard project →"
beats.say: Registering the project lands the operator on its page. Nothing linked here a moment ago — the route exists because the button was pressed, which is how every one of forge’s operator flows works.

do.with: A throwaway project proving the story runner can fill a form and press a button.
